clue.text: Old copper a Scotsman friend of Pythias

parts.note: d was the abbreviation for the old British penny, a copper coin
mon is the Scots form of man, so a Scotsman is a mon

explanation.surface: A retired policeman and a Scot turn out to be companions of a figure from Greek legend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend Damon offered his life as surety for his friend Pythias; the pair stand for loyal friendship. D is the old penny (pre-1971 British currency).
explanation.definitionFit: Damon and Pythias are the proverbial pair of devoted friends in the Greek tale of Syracuse.

clue.text: Adder's peak period?

parts.note: an adder here is not a snake but someone who sums figures, and the peak of such a person is the top of the warmest season

explanation.surface: A naturalist asks when the snake is most active.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adder' suggests a snake; read it as one who adds, a summer, and its peak (height) gives the phrase meaning midsummer, the peak period of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the hottest, fullest point of the warm season, its peak period.

clue.text: See 2
Ask for a hand in a tender way

definitions.meaning: to ask for someone's hand is to make an offer of marriage
to tender is to put forward or offer, as a motion or plan is put forward

explanation.surface: A suitor gently asks for a lady's hand in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are offering: a marriage offer, and putting forward a suggestion for consideration.

clue.text: Excited as Moscow was in 1812?

definitions.meaning: flushed with excitement, glowing with feeling
Moscow burned for days after Napoleon's army entered it in 1812

explanation.surface: A history question about Moscow's state during Napoleon's invasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing describes a face flushed with excitement and, literally, a city lit up by fire.

clue.text: How you're pictured in the old family album

definitions.text: How you're pictured in the old family album

parts.words: How you're pictured in the old family album
parts.note: old photographs show people as they used to be, and the same phrase is a drill-sergeant's order to return to the previous position

explanation.surface: Someone leafs through old photographs of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is also a military command cancelling the last order, which the surface hides behind the photo album.
explanation.definitionFit: An old photograph shows a person in their former state, how they used to look.

clue.text: Put word around after changing place in Eire

indicators.note: the word 'word' is placed around the other letters, opened between its first letter and the rest
changing tells us the letters of 'after' are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to wrap a word around something after altering a place name in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is a link here. 'changing' rearranges the second word and 'around' wraps the first round it. Waterford is a city and county in the Republic of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterford is a port city in the south-east of the Irish Republic.

clue.text: Gateshead girl a product of 7

parts.note: read as Gate's head, the first letter of the word gate
lass is a northern English word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman from Gateshead, a town in north-east England, came out of an Irish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town on the Tyne in north-east England, where 'lass' is everyday speech; split as Gate's head it gives G. Item 7 is WATERFORD, famous for its cut crystal.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterford is renowned for its cut crystal tableware, a famous Irish export.

clue.text: It has eminence in Co. Meath, thanks to an artist

definitions.text: It has eminence in Co. Meath

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A place prominent in an Irish county owes its fame to a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eminence' means a hill: the Hill of Tara in County Meath was the seat of the ancient High Kings of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hill of Tara is a historic rise in County Meath, so the site has an eminence.

clue.text: Spring should be forward in this event

definitions.text: Spring should be forward in this event

parts.words: Spring should be forward in this event
parts.note: the spring is an athlete's leap, which in this field event must carry far ahead rather than high

explanation.surface: A gardener hopes for an early season this year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season and 'forward' like early growth; read as a leap that should go a long way forward, it names the athletics event.
explanation.definitionFit: In this athletics event a competitor leaps forward from a take-off board as far as possible.

clue.text: Colourless gas surrounding a Spanish region

indicators.note: surrounding means the gas wraps itself round the single letter

parts.note: argon is an inert colourless gas

explanation.surface: An invisible gas envelops part of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Aragon is an autonomous community in north-east Spain, once a kingdom.

clue.text: To make a note of it takes me back

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: takes me back means the word me is written backwards after it

explanation.surface: Writing something down brings back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ME into EM. As a verb ITEM is an old word meaning to jot down or list.
explanation.definitionFit: As an archaic verb it means to set down in a list or memorandum.

clue.text: Part of the main but not in the deep

definitions.text: Part of the main but not in the deep

parts.words: Part of the main but not in the deep
parts.note: the main is the sea, and the stretch of it that is not deep lies near the shore

explanation.surface: Something is mainly included but kept out of the deep end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is a poetic word for the sea, and 'the deep' is too: the part of the sea that is not deep water is near the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: These are stretches of sea with little depth of water.

clue.text: Dry-heated in order to lose moisture

indicators.note: in order says the letters are put into proper order, a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Something is heated dry so that it loses its water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order to' reads as purpose; 'in order' is the anagram signal and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry out is to have water removed or given up.

clue.text: Supporter on the blower in Italy

parts.note: a leg supports a body or a table
a horn is blown

explanation.surface: Someone's backer is on the telephone in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The blower' is British slang for the telephone, but here it is something blown, a HORN. Leghorn is the old English name for Livorno, the Tuscan port.
explanation.definitionFit: Leghorn is the traditional English name for Livorno, a port city on Italy's west coast.

clue.text: Enclosed, we turn on her &and hit out

indicators.note: in a down clue placing one piece on another puts it after, below it
turn means the word we is reversed in place
out signals that the letters of hit are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gang turn on a woman and hit out at her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses one word, 'on' sets it below the other in this down clue, and 'out' scrambles the last. 'Herewith' in a letter means 'enclosed with this'.
explanation.definitionFit: In business letters it means accompanying this document, as in material sent along with it.

clue.text: Defence a mole provides

definitions.meaning: a wall or rampart giving protection
a mole is a stone breakwater, which shelters a harbour from the sea

explanation.surface: An animal burrowing underground supplies protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' suggests the burrowing animal; here it is a harbour breakwater, which acts as a sea wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are a protective wall: a rampart, and a breakwater against waves.

clue.text: Socially acceptable party measure of wetness

parts.note: U means upper-class, socially acceptable, in British usage
a do is a party
a meter is an instrument that measures

explanation.surface: A respectable party sets a measure of how damp things are.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class (acceptable) is a British convention from the 1950s 'U and non-U' debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain gauge records how much rain has fallen.

clue.text: Teaches a way to plunder

indicators.note: a way suggests the letters are taken one way among many, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shows another person how to rob.
explanation.walkthrough: As an old verb, escheat meant to confiscate property, hence to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To escheat was to seize property as forfeit, an act of taking goods by right.

clue.text: Main outlets of relief from an odd dry spell in a county

indicators.note: in means the scrambled word sits inside the county

parts.note: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county

indicators.note: odd says the letters of dry are set strangely

explanation.surface: Relief arrives from a strange drought in an English shire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' scrambles the short word and 'in' puts it inside Hants, short for Hampshire, a county in southern England. 'Main' is a water main, not the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire plugs are points where water can be drawn off from a water main.

clue.text: She's sound as a bell

indicators.note: this word says the answer is heard rather than seen: it sounds like the word it governs

parts.note: a knell is the tolling of a bell

explanation.surface: A woman is said to be in perfect health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound as a bell' is an idiom for in perfect health, but the pronunciation of a bell's toll, KNELL, gives a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nell is a woman's name, so she is the person referred to.

clue.text: Hops in her prepared for a drink

definitions.text: Hops in her prepared for a drink

parts.words: Hops in her prepared for a drink
parts.note: hops are the plant used in brewing beer, and they are dried in a kiln before brewing

explanation.surface: A lively woman bounces about getting ready for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hops' looks like jumping; it is the plant, dried in this kiln before brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a kiln for drying hops before brewing, so the hops inside are made ready for beer.

clue.text: Reassure a number in solitary confinement

indicators.note: confinement means the single word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: sole means single, alone
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone tries to cheer a prisoner kept in a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... confinement' splits round 'solitary': the A and the Roman hundred are shut inside the word for alone, as a prisoner sits in a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: To console someone is to comfort them in trouble.

clue.text: It's all right as a change in C Honshu

indicators.note: change signals that the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: OK means all right

explanation.surface: A traveller reports that all is well after a switch in central Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges OK + AS + A. Osaka is a major city in central Honshu, Japan's main island.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a great port city on Japan's main island.

clue.text: Sounds a brutal kind of yarn

indicators.note: Sounds says the word is pronounced like the one entered

parts.note: brutal means cruel

explanation.surface: Someone describes a savage tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' suggests a story; it is the woollen thread used in embroidery.
explanation.definitionFit: This is fine worsted wool used for embroidery.

clue.text: Happy-go-lucky, but it's said he wasn't so well off

indicators.note: it's said marks a phrase spoken aloud that matches the written word

parts.note: a man not so well off had less, so he'd less

explanation.surface: A carefree man is said to have been poorer once.
explanation.definitionFit: A carefree person takes no care or notice of risks.

clue.text: Explain a condition

definitions.meaning: to set out or declare in words
a ... of affairs or the situation something is in

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to set out in words; the other is the situation or shape something is in.

clue.text: Suitable confection for a hen party?

definitions.text: Suitable confection for a hen party?

parts.words: Suitable confection for a hen party?
parts.note: a hen party is a woman's pre-wedding night out, but a real hen lays eggs, so the fitting cake is a stacked sponge

explanation.surface: Someone plans a cake for a bride-to-be's night out.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a British pre-wedding celebration for women; taking 'hen' literally, the cake suits a bird that lays.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cake made of stacked sponge tiers with filling between.
